title: [3/6/2023] The use of water by four different countries
prompt: The table below shows water use for different purposes in four countries. The use of water by four different countries (%) (no specific time period). Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the proportions of water usage for domestic, industrial and agricultural purposes in four different countries.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, agriculture accounts for the highest percentage of water consumption in Egypt and Saudi Arabia, while industry is the dominant user in Canada and New Zealand. Additionally, domestic use represents the smallest share across all four nations.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding Egypt and Saudi Arabia, these two countries allocate the majority of their water to agriculture, at 82% and 64% respectively. Their industrial water usage shows a notable difference, with Saudi Arabia's figure of 30% being three times higher than Egypt's 10%. As for domestic consumption, both countries record single-digit percentages, with Egypt at 8% and Saudi Arabia slightly lower at 6%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In terms of the remaining countries, Canada and New Zealand demonstrate contrasting patterns, with industry being their primary water consumer. Canada's industrial usage is significantly higher at 70%, compared to New Zealand's 46%. Agricultural water consumption in New Zealand stands at 44%, which is more than four times higher than Canada's mere 10%. Domestic use in these two countries is relatively higher than in the Middle Eastern nations, with Canada recording 20% and New Zealand 10%.
